_doc: Storyboard of The Pantry Key: the source of truth for every line of the game (rooms/*.ts follow it). Shape: { title, intro?, boards: [{ id, title, room, goal, arrival?: Line[], panels: [{ id, title, action?, lines: Line[], sfx?: string[] }], hints: string[] (shell phone, in puzzle order), talks: { <character id>: [{ topic, lines: Line[] }] }, reactions?: [{ action, lines: Line[] }] }] }. Line = { who, text }: who is a character id ('hero' = Pixel), 'action' = what the player does, 'stage' = a stage direction. Panel ids are stable: review notes are keyed by them (tools/pages/storyboard.ts).
title: The Pantry Key
intro: Pixel the grey cat wants the sardines. Grandma locked them in the pantry and lost the key. Three rooms, two minigames, one sealed ending.

boards.title: Opening and tutorial
boards.goal: Guess what is in the pantry, then learn Look at, Talk to, Pick up.

lines.text: Pixel! Bad news. The sardines are locked in the pantry...
...and I lost the key.
Wait. What is really in that pantry?
Sardines. Obviously.
A mouse. A big one.
Nothing at all. It is a trap.
We will see when it is open, fluffball.
First, LOOK AT the pantry cupboard.
The pantry cupboard. The sardines live in there.

panels.title: Guide: talk
panels.action: Talk to Grandma: Where is the key?

lines.text: Now TALK TO Grandma. Ask about the key.
Grandpa had it last. He is in the garden, fixing the pipes.
Go through the big window. Mind the roses.
The garden is unlocked (toast: New on the map: the garden).
Take my shell phone. Talk into it if you get stuck.
PICK UP the shell phone on the table.
Got it. It smells like the sea.
Garden. Grandpa. Key. Sardines. Easy.

boards.title: Grandma's house
boards.goal: Find the market token in Grandpa's armchair, then go to the garden.

lines.text: Behind the cushion... a market token!
And Grandpa's remote. I will leave that one. Too much TV.
Just crumbs. Old crumbs.

panels.title: To the garden
panels.action: Use the garden window (or the map, by car)

panels.title: Grandpa comes home (event + moving character)
panels.action: Triggered by the market: the key is found

lines.text: The market emits key_found; the game listener moves Grandpa (and his armchair) to the house. Biscuit stretches every seven seconds on his own (script).
Pixel! I beat you home. The armchair is faster than it looks.
The door jumps twice (animation frames), the latch clicks on frame 1.
Locked. I need the key.

panels.title: Biscuit, playable (switch)
panels.action: Switch to Biscuit (bag button), use teacup

lines.text: A second playable cat: the switch button next to the map. Biscuit has his own bag; Pixel can give him things.
Lukewarm tea. Biscuit approves.
Empty. Biscuit regrets nothing.

hints: Ask me where the key is, sweetie.
Grandpa's armchair eats everything. Look behind the cushion.
Open the armchair, sweetie. Or pull it.
Grandpa is in the garden. Go through the big window.
Something came out of the water tank, no? Read it, then call Lou.
The key is at the market. Open the map.
You have the key! Use it on the pantry cupboard.

lines.text: Grandpa had it last. He is in the garden, fixing the pipes.
Go through the big window. Mind the roses.
Sardines. If we find the key.
(2nd time) Still sardines.
(then) Pixel. Sardines. Go.
Because a certain cat opens cupboards. A certain grey cat.
Biscuit. Definitely Biscuit.

grandma.topic: I found the key! (with the key)

lines.text: Then what are you waiting for? Open the pantry!

grandma.topic: Can I have a cuddle? (every character)

lines.text: Come here, fluffball. Purr purr.
A cat with a key. I had to see this.
It walked. I only steered.
Armchairs. Full of secrets.
Never pull a cat. Cat law, article one.
Biscuit purrs and goes back to sleep.
Hot tea and cat paws. No.
Heavy. And it judges me.
Locked. I need the key.
The hall. The vacuum cleaner lives there. Our sworn enemy.
Grandpa. He came home for the sardines. With his armchair.
He is "guarding the pantry". With his eyes closed.
Pixel. Smaller than me. Faster than me. Fine.
My little brother. Still planning. Always planning.

boards.title: The garden
boards.goal: Drain the water tank, read the note in the sock, call Lou.

arrival.text: Pixel! Did you come to help me fix the pipes?
I came for a key. And sardines.

lines.text: A pipe! Grandpa will not miss it. He is asleep.
The tap is stuck. The water needs another way out. A pipe, maybe?

panels.title: Pipes minigame
panels.action: Use pipe with water tank → minigame pipes

lines.text: Tap a pipe to turn it. Bring the water to the mushrooms.
The mushrooms are drinking!
The tank drains (prop state), the screen shakes, Grandpa looks surprised. A sock appears. The pipe stays in the bag, greyed.
Look! Something at the bottom!
That is not a key. That is a sock.
A wet sock. With a note inside!
It says: "Borrowed the key to copy it. Lou."
Lou, the neighbour! Call Lou with the shell phone.
Shell phone, call Lou!
Lou speaking. Oh, hi Pixel!
Lou! You have Grandma's key!
Had. I am at the market. Come and get it!
LOU! Your lantern is ready!
Hurry up, it is busy here. Bye!
The market is unlocked (toast: New on the map: the market). The trip is by plane.

hints: There is a spare pipe on the ground. Take it, sweetie.
Use the pipe on the water tank.
Pipe. Tank. Together. Go!
Something came out of the tank. Look at it.
Talk into my shell phone and call Lou.
Lou is at the market. Open the map.
Come home with that key, sweetie!

lines.text: The key? It fell in the water tank. Plop.
Drain it. But the tap is stuck.
(2nd time) Still stuck? Try a pipe. Pipes are good with water.
(then, laughing) Ha! A cat doing plumbing. I love it.

grandpa.topic: There was no key in the tank! (after draining)

lines.text: No? Only a sock? Read the sock. Socks always have something to say.
It wanted some sun. Armchairs need vitamins too.
Yes. With my eyes closed. I am an expert.
A wet sock. Cat rule number two: never touch wet things.
Dogs. Street. No.
He does not move. He has roots.

boards.title: The market
boards.goal: Win the bouquet with the token, trade it for the key.

panels.title: The deposit
panels.action: Talk to Lou: Where is the pantry key?

lines.text: Ah. I left it with the seller. A deposit for that lantern.
Pay for the lantern and the key is yours.
That is MY key! Well, Grandma's.
Technically, it is his now. Deposits are serious business.
Fine. How do I pay?
He loves tokens. And flowers. Mostly flowers today.

panels.title: Token for a game
panels.action: Give market token to the seller

lines.text: A token? Today I only take flowers. For... reasons.
Pick the right three flowers from my bucket, and the token will do.

panels.title: Pick minigame
panels.action: Pick the poppy, the sunflower, the lavender (the nettle is a trap)

lines.text: The seller wants a red flower with a black heart.
Now a big yellow one that looks at the sun.
Last one: purple, and it smells like soap.
Ouch! A nettle. Not romantic at all.
A perfect bouquet!
Beautiful! I put it on the stall for you.
For the seller. Not for eating. Sadly.
For me? ...Oh no. Today is my wedding anniversary!
I forgot! You saved me, little cat.
Here: the key. The lantern is paid.
Yes! My lantern!
And my sardines!
Between the player's actions, Lou walks to the middle stall and back, until the bouquet is given.
Toast when the key is found: "Grandpa went home. With the armchair."
The market is one and a half screens wide: the camera follows Pixel. Looking at the alley pans to the far stalls, then back.
More stalls, further down. Also no sardines.
A whole market and not one fish.

hints: Talk to Lou about the key, sweetie.
Did you search Grandpa's armchair at home? It eats tokens.
Give your market token to the seller.
Your bouquet is on the stall. Take it.
Give the bouquet to the seller.
You have the key! Come home and open the pantry.

lines.text: Ah. I left it with the seller. A deposit for that lantern.

neighbor.topic: Why did you take the key?

lines.text: To make a copy. In case Grandma loses it.
She did lose it.
See? I was right.
For my garage. I fix things at night. Like a bat with a wrench.
The key is Lou's deposit. Pay for the lantern, and it is yours.
Tokens are fine. Flowers are better. Today, flowers are much better.
Sardines? No. Spices, teapots, lanterns.
Worst. Market. Ever.
No reason. Definitely no reason. What day is it?
Paws off! That lantern is sold. Almost.
Opens the map.

panels.title: Open! (cutscene)
panels.action: Use pantry key with pantry cupboard

lines.text: Open! Sardines! Hello, my little friends.
Pixel eats. Biscuit wakes up. The key stays in the bag, greyed.
Mrrp? Did someone say sardines?
Ha! Two cats, one tin. Share, you two.
Fine. Half. Ish.
Scratch ticket (text from the sealed file), confetti.
Well done, Pixel. Best breakfast ever.
Best. Breakfast. Ever.
Final card: headline and the verdict on the opening guess (ending.guess), Play again, Credits.
